37566-natural-history-of-the-ornate-box-.title: Terrapene ornata ornata Agassiz
37566-natural-history-of-the-ornate-box-.creator: Unknown
37566-natural-history-of-the-ornate-box-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Turtles of the genus _Terrapene_ belong to the Emyidae, a family comprising chiefly aquatic and semiaquatic species. _Terrapene_, nevertheless, is adapted for terrestrial existence and differs from all other North American emyids in having a hinged and movable plastron and a down-turned (although often notched) maxillary beak. _Emydoidea blandingi_, the only other North American emyid with a hinged plastron, lacks a down-turned beak.

40357-four-months-afoot-in-spain.title: Four Months Afoot In Spain
40357-four-months-afoot-in-spain.creator: Unknown
40357-four-months-afoot-in-spain.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. in May that I mounted to my lodgings in Hartley Hall, rollicksome with the information that I should soon be free from professional duties a full four months. Where I preferred to spend that term of freedom was easily decided.

arxiv-2004-10269.title: The Sum of Squares function in the ring ℤ n \mathbb{Z}_{n}
arxiv-2004-10269.creator: Rob Burns
arxiv-2004-10269.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Rob Burns. We consider the sum of squares function in the ring ℤ n \mathbb{Z}_{n} . We determine formulae in a number of cases when n n is a power of a prime. 1 Introduction The representation of elements of a ring as a sum of squares (or more generally as a sum of powers) is a very large and old subject. In the following we attempt to give a flavour of the type of questions that have been studied.

arxiv-2111-03125.title: Secure Machine Learning in the Cloud Using One Way Scrambling by Deconvolution
arxiv-2111-03125.creator: Yiftach Savransky, Roni Mateless, Gilad Katz
arxiv-2111-03125.description: Abstract Cloud-based machine learning services (CMLS) enable organizations to take advantage of advanced models that are pre-trained on large quantities of data. The main shortcoming of using these services, however, is the difficulty of keeping the transmitted data private and secure.

arxiv-2111-07868.title: Tracking People with 3D Representations
arxiv-2111-07868.creator: Jathushan Rajasegaran, Georgios Pavlakos, Angjoo Kanazawa, Jitendra Malik
arxiv-2111-07868.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jathushan Rajasegaran, Georgios Pavlakos, Angjoo Kanazawa, Jitendra Malik. We present a novel approach for tracking multiple people in video. Unlike past approaches which employ 2D representations, we focus on using 3D representations of people, located in three-dimensional space. To this end, we develop a method, Human Mesh and Appearance Recovery (HMAR) which in addition to extracting the 3D geometry of the person as a SMPL mesh, also extracts appearance as a texture map on the triangles of the mesh.

arxiv-2303-15950.title: A Source Separation Approach to Temporal Graph Modelling for Computer Networks
arxiv-2303-15950.creator: Corentin Larroche
arxiv-2303-15950.description: Abstract Detecting malicious activity within an enterprise computer network can be framed as a temporal link prediction task: given a sequence of graphs representing communications between hosts over time, the goal is to predict which edges should—or should not—occur in the future.

arxiv-2306-03646.title: Dance Generation by Sound Symbolic Words DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Make sure to enter the correct conference title from your rights confirmation emai; June 03–05, 2018; Woodstock, NY Woodstock ’18: ACM Symposium on Neural Gaze Detection, June 03–05, 2018, Woodstock, NY Price: 15.00 ISBN: 978-
arxiv-2306-03646.creator: Miki Okamura, Naruya Kondo, Tatsuki Fushimi, Maki Sakamoto, Yoichi Ochiai
arxiv-2306-03646.description: Abstract . This study introduces a novel approach to generate dance motions using onomatopoeia as input, with the aim of enhancing creativity and diversity in dance generation. Unlike text and music, onomatopoeia conveys rhythm and meaning through abstract word expressions without constraints on expression and without need for specialized knowledge.

arxiv-2404-05090.title: How Bad is Training on Synthetic Data? A Statistical Analysis of Language Model Collapse
arxiv-2404-05090.creator: Mohamed El Amine Seddik, Suei-Wen Chen, Soufiane Hayou, Pierre Youssef, Merouane Debbah
arxiv-2404-05090.description: Abstract The phenomenon of model collapse, introduced in ( Shumailov et al., 2023 ) , refers to the deterioration in performance that occurs when new models are trained on synthetic data generated from previously trained models. This recursive training loop makes the tails of the original distribution disappear, thereby making future-generation models forget about the initial (real) distribution.

arxiv-2503-02655.title: Quantum Geometry insights in Deep Learning
arxiv-2503-02655.creator: Noémie C. Combe
arxiv-2503-02655.description: Abstract . In this paper, we explore the fundamental role of the Monge–Ampère equation in deep learning, particularly in the context of Boltzmann machines and energy-based models. We first review the structure of Boltzmann learning and its relation to free energy minimization.

arxiv-2504-06757.title: Local equations describe unreasonably efficient stochastic algorithms in random K-SAT
arxiv-2504-06757.creator: David Machado, Jonathan González-García, Roberto Mulet
arxiv-2504-06757.description: Abstract Despite significant advances in characterizing the highly nonconvex landscapes of constraint satisfaction problems, the good performance of certain algorithms in solving hard combinatorial optimization tasks remains poorly understood. This gap in understanding stems largely from the lack of theoretical tools for analyzing their out-of-equilibrium dynamics.

arxiv-2505-18702.title: Eccentric millisecond pulsar + subdwarf B star from rotationally delayed accretion-induced-collapse scenario Eccentric millisecond pulsar + subdwarf B star from rotationally delayed accretion-induced-collapse scenario – References 2018
arxiv-2505-18702.creator: Xiang-Cun Meng
arxiv-2505-18702.description: Abstract Neutron star + helium star systems are attracting more and more attentions. Following the rotationally delayed accretion-induced-collapse (RD-AIC) scenario, I predict that there could be eccentric millisecond pulsar + subdwarf B (MSP + sdB), at least eccentric neutron star + subdwarf B (NS + sdB) systems in the Galaxy.

arxiv-2506-06539.title: Beyond Facts: Evaluating Intent Hallucination in Large Language Models
arxiv-2506-06539.creator: Yijie Hao, Haofei Yu, Jiaxuan You
arxiv-2506-06539.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yijie Hao, Haofei Yu, Jiaxuan You. When exposed to complex queries containing multiple conditions, today’s large language models (LLMs) tend to produce responses that only partially satisfy the query while neglecting certain conditions. We therefore introduce the concept of Intent Hallucination . In this phenomenon, LLMs either omit (neglecting to address certain parts) or misinterpret (responding to invented query parts) elements of the given query, leading to intent hallucinated generation.

arxiv-2508-06326.title: A “Good Regulator Theorem” for Embodied Agents
arxiv-2508-06326.creator: Nathaniel Virgo, Martin Biehl, Manuel Baltieri, Matteo Capucci
arxiv-2508-06326.description: Abstract In a classic paper, Conant and Ashby claimed that “every good regulator of a system must be a model of that system.” Artificial Life has produced many examples of systems that perform tasks with apparently no model in sight; these suggest Conant and Ashby’s theorem doesn’t easily generalise beyond its restricted setup.

arxiv-2601-16431.title: Sequential Experimental Designs for Kriging Model
arxiv-2601-16431.creator: Ruonan Zheng, Min-Qian Liu, Yongdao Zhou, Xuan Chen
arxiv-2601-16431.description: Abstract Computer experiments have become an indispensable alternative to complex physical and engineering experiments. The Kriging model is the most widely used surrogate model, with the core goal of minimizing the discrepancy between the surrogate and true models across the entire experimental domain.

pmc-10716662.title: How visuomotor predictability and task demands affect tactile sensitivity on a moving limb during object interaction in a virtual environment
pmc-10716662.creator: Meaghan McManus, Immo Schütz, Dimitris Voudouris, Katja Fiehler
pmc-10716662.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Tactile sensitivity is decreased on a moving limb compared to the same static limb. This tactile suppression likely reflects an interplay between sensorimotor predictions and sensory feedback. Here, we examined how visuomotor predictability influences tactile suppression. Participants were instructed to hit an approaching virtual object, with the object either never rotating, or always rotating, or rotating unpredictably, prompting related movement adjustments.

pmc-10727644.title: Does the VHL polymorphisms rs779805 and rs1642742 affect renal cell carcinoma susceptibility, prognosis and survival in Central European population?
pmc-10727644.creator: Magdalena Chrabańska, Nikola Szweda-Gandor, Bogna Drozdzowska
pmc-10727644.description: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is a common malignant tumor of the urinary system. The von Hippel–Lindau (VHL) tumor suppressor gene play an essential role in the tumorigenic pathway of clear cell RCC (ccRCC). This study was aimed to clarify the influence of VHL polymorphisms on ccRCC susceptibility and survival in Central European population.

pmc-11357800.title: Protocol for isolating immune cells from human gastric muscularis propria for single-cell analysis
pmc-11357800.creator: Shefaa AlAsfoor, Cheryl E Bernard, Erik Jessen, Vernadette A Simon, Fariborz Rakhshan, Gianluca Cipriani, Linda C Hsi, Jack A Patraw, Kari J Carothers, Julie S Lau, Samantha J McDonough, Surendra Dasari, Gianrico Farrugia, Madhusudan Grover
pmc-11357800.description: SummaryUnderstanding the diversity of gastrointestinal (GI) immune cells, especially in the muscularis propria, is crucial for understanding their role in the maintenance of enteric neurons and smooth muscle and their contribution to GI motility. Here, we present a detailed protocol for isolating single immune cells from the human gastric muscularis propria.

pmc-11461840.title: 5-Fluorouracil induces apoptosis in nutritional deprived hepatocellular carcinoma through mitochondrial damage
pmc-11461840.creator: Ankita Dutta, Anuja Chakraborty, Tulika Ghosh, Anoop Kumar
pmc-11461840.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) is the leading chemotherapeutic drug used to treat hepatocellular carcinoma, one of the major cancer diseases after atherosclerosis. Because of chemo-resistance, the success rate of treatment declines with time due to continuous drug exposure. Though autophagy induction is majorly responsible for acquired resistance, the exact role of this evolutionary conserved mechanism is unknown in cancer cell survival and suppression.

pmc-11530791.title: Physical and electrochemical performances of novel tellurium composite films as anode applications in energy storage systems
pmc-11530791.creator: Md Masud Rana, Mohammad Asaduzzaman Chowdhury, Md. Jonaidul Alam, Md. Rifat Khandaker, Yusuf Ali
pmc-11530791.description: Portable electronic devices and electric cars use lithium-ion batteries, but clumping lithium alloys limit their lifespan. Due to their strong electronic conductivity, volumetric capacity, and high energy density, researchers are conducting research on electrochemical metal cells utilizing tellurium for high-performance batteries. Theoretically, lithium-tellurium batteries can improve energy densities three times more than lithium-ion batteries.

pmc-11619467.title: SMILE and ICL implantation on the ocular surface and meibomian glands in patients with postoperative myopia
pmc-11619467.creator: Juan Yao, Jianghong Feng, Weijie Li, Chang Liu, Yanlei Li, Xiaoying Wang
pmc-11619467.description: BackgroundObjectively compare the changes in ocular surface parameters in myopic patients who have undergone either SMILE or Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL V4c) surgery.MethodsThis prospective cohort study enrolled 32 patients (32 eyes) undergoing SMILE surgery and 35 patients (35 eyes) receiving ICL V4c intraocular lenses. Examinations were performed at preoperative, 1-week, 1-month, and 3-month postoperative time points.

pmc-12409913.title: Chronic pain and quality of life among people with whiplash injury in Iceland
pmc-12409913.creator: Hafdís Skúladóttir, Gudmundur Kristjan Óskarsson, Thorbjorg Jónsdóttir, Sigfridur Inga Karlsdóttir, Eva Halapi
pmc-12409913.description: The purpose was to examine the participants’ pain severity, pain interference, health-related quality of life (HRQoL), needs, access and use of healthcare services, and the difference between those reporting whiplash injury ( >12 months) with and without chronic pain and those without whiplash injury but with chronic pain. This is a cross-sectional cohort study.

pmc-12417271.title: Gallbladder Squamous Cell Carcinoma with Diffuse β-hCG Expression: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
pmc-12417271.creator: Shengliang He, Dustin E Bosch, Alan Hemming
pmc-12417271.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). PurposeGallbladder squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is a rare subtype of gallbladder malignancy, comprising only 1–4% of cases. Ectopic expression of β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) has been described in various epithelial cancers and is associated with aggressive behavior.

pmc-12501428.title: Functional insights into Solo-Cas4 in Methanosarcina mazei Gö1
pmc-12501428.creator: Luise Rentz, Lisa Hellwig, Sabine Schneider, Ruth A Schmitz
pmc-12501428.description: Solo-Cas4 homologs are Cas4-family proteins found outside of canonical CRISPR–Cas operons. Here, we present the biochemical characterization of Solo-Cas4 from Methanosarcina mazei Gö1. We found significantly upregulated solo-cas4 transcript levels during stationary phase, while remaining constant under oxygen exposure, temperature shifts, high salt conditions or virus challenge.

pmc-12566809.title: Characterization and Biological Characteristics of Alternaria, Botryosphaeria, Pestalotiopsis, and Trichothecium Species Associated with Postharvest Loquat Fruit Rot in Yunnan, China
pmc-12566809.creator: Jian-Wei Guo, Chun-Lian Yang, Beng-Zha Dong, Rong-Chuan Tian, Min Yang, Lifang Li, Penghua Gao, Su-Yue Zhou, Murad Muhammad, Yu Bu, Junbo Zhang, Chui-Si Kong, Lei Yu, Manuel Avilés
pmc-12566809.description: Postharvest diseases caused by various fungal pathogens pose a significant threat to fruit quality, storage, and market value, making their identification and biological characterization essential for effective management strategies. This study examines the morphological and phylogenetic characteristics of Alternaria, Botryosphaeria, Pestalotiopsis, and Trichothecium species associated with loquat fruit rot in Yunnan, China.

pmc-12671354.title: Modeling liquid-liquid phase separation and its impact on proteasomal substrate degradation
pmc-12671354.creator: Di Wu, Qi Ouyang, Hongli Wang
pmc-12671354.description: The proteasome, central to ubiquitin-proteasome mediated degradation of substrate proteins, undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) during substrate processing. However, the mechanisms governing proteasomal LLPS and its functional interplay with degradation dynamics remain elusive. Here, we developed a reaction-diffusion model with thermodynamic constraints to quantitatively characterize proteasome-associated LLPS mediated by the substrate-shuttling factor Radiation-sensitive 23 homolog B (RAD23B).

pmc-12723956.title: Multi-omics reveals FAT10 as an immunometabolic survival factor rewiring global metabolism in cancer
pmc-12723956.creator: Jun Yan Loh, Jianhong Ching, Jean-Paul Kovalik, Shuaichen Liu, Lee Jin Lim, Samuel S Chong, Caroline G L Lee
pmc-12723956.description: BackgroundFAT10 is an inflammation-induced oncogene highly overexpressed across multiple cancers. As a ubiquitin-like protein, it regulates interacting proteins by destabilizing, stabilizing or delocalizing them. Despite its extensive influence on targets from various cellular pathways, prior studies largely focused on interrogating individual protein interactions, limiting our understanding of FAT10’s broader oncogenic role.

pmc-12813033.title: The roles of cognitive and motivational imagery on flow: a multiple indicators multiple causes approach
pmc-12813033.creator: Seungmin Lee, Jun-Phil Uhm
pmc-12813033.description: IntroductionWhile mental training in coaching often targets Flow, it may overlook its multidimensional nature and distinct imagery pathways, limiting effective interventions for athletic performance. This study examined the effects of five imagery abilities—Skill, Strategy, Goal, Affect, and Mastery—on nine Flow dimensions in sport using a Multiple Indicators Multiple Causes (MIMIC) model.

pmc-12964894.title: Towards tuberculosis elimination in people with HIV on antiretroviral therapy: evidence from a two-decade nationwide cohort in Spain
pmc-12964894.creator: Roser Navarro-Soler, Alfonso Muriel, Chiara Fanciulli, José I Bernardino, Carmen Sáez, Javier Zamora, Borja M Fernandez-Felix, Alejandro G García-Ruíz de Morales, Eva Poveda, Álvaro Mena de Cea, Javier Martínez-Sanz, Santiago Moreno, Sergio Serrano-Villar
pmc-12964894.description: BackgroundTuberculosis (TB) incidence among people with HIV (PWH) has fallen in many high-income settings, yet residual risk persists, and tools to identify those still vulnerable are limited. This study aimed to evaluate TB incidence trends, identify risk factors, and develop a predictive score in PWH in Spain.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study using the Spanish AIDS Research Network (CoRIS).

pmc-13230550.title: Wafer-level meta-aspheric lenses for compact wide-FOV NIR imaging
pmc-13230550.creator: Eunji Lee, Junsuk Rho
pmc-13230550.description: A meta-aspheric lens fabricated at the wafer-level achieves a 101.5° field of view, a 3.39 mm total track length, and an F/1.64 aperture within a volume of 0.02 cm3, enabling compact and scalable near-infrared imaging. Near-infrared (NIR) imaging is now integral to consumer and biomedical systems, spanning AR eye tracking, biometric authentication, and subcutaneous vascular imaging1–4.
